page: Microsoft Azure D4alds_v6 is a virtual machine configuration belonging to the Daldv6 family, powered by AMD EPYC 9V74 processors running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. It features 8.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, and includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for premium remote storage. There are no dedicated GPUs attached, and network provisioning includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct compute characteristics driven by the high CPU clock speed. Single-core performance is robust, with the instance placing in the top 25 percent for both stress-ng single-core execution (3079.18) and Geekbench single-core compute (2078.0), alongside strong results in text processing benchmarks. Multi-core performance aligns with the middle 50 percent, delivering a multi-threaded stress-ng score of 6151.67 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4740.0. The underlying processor includes vector acceleration features such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware-assisted AES and SHA cryptography extensions.

The constrained memory footprint and bandwidth present measurable performance tradeoffs. Memory bandwidth testing demonstrates lower-tier throughput, recording 37.74 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and a PassMark memory score of 1746.14. These bottlenecks contribute to reduced efficiency in memory-intensive operations, including database transactions, Redis SET operations (5.88 million ops/sec), Clang compilation, and 7B-parameter LLM inference. In contrast, workloads with smaller memory footprints achieve stable middle-tier results, such as static web serving at 6.47 GB/sec and small-model inference (135M) at 158.72 tokens/sec.

Given its high clock speeds, bundled 236 GB local NVMe storage, and lower memory ratio, the D4alds_v6 offers practical hardware efficiency for CPU-bound tasks that do not demand extensive RAM. It serves effectively for batch compute processing, microservices, front-end web serving, and lightweight application tiers requiring fast temporary disk access.
description: Microsoft Azure D4alds_v6 is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of memory and 236 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V on the x86_64 architecture, this instance emphasizes high single-thread CPU performance, registering strong benchmark marks in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. Due to its reduced memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, memory throughput and database transaction metrics score lower relative to larger configurations. Workloads requiring extensive in-memory caching or deep language-model processing encounter architectural bottlenecks, whereas lightweight web serving, command-line utilities, text parsing, and distributed worker nodes benefit directly from the fast CPU clock rates and fast local scratch storage without incurring excessive infrastructure resource overhead.
